goal: Redesign BloomRender frontend using PoseWear interaction references and the taste skill, with a clear person/clothing/pose try-on workflow.

reference.inspection: Live gallery and studio plus README, studio and styling source. Independently implemented grouping, role-based inputs and navigation; no upstream code or pictures copied.

implementation: One shared home/tool navigation, primary try-on/material entries and grouped tool drawer; existing routes and three themes retained.
Homepage uses a split live-editor preview, task-first actions, consistent grid and reachable provider/demo controls on short screens.
Try-on uses ordered person, clothing and optional pose steps with actual selected-reference board. Advanced settings, prompts, drafts and recipes are secondary.
Inputs stay editable after generation. Previous results survive editing, replacement progress and failure. Comparison/retry uses generation-time input snapshots.
New sessions preserve the original background and use the original style; explicit existing recipe/history settings remain unchanged.
32 atomic material IDs appear as 11 grouped cards. Paired poses offer camera views and optional depth representations; favorites, recent items, basket, viewer and exact recipe IDs remain.
Independent person/composition revisions prevent immediate person uploads from discarding a pending material transfer while keeping newer reference edits protected.
Clipboard denial preserves valid recipe links for manual copying.

This is the interactive try-on form, not a marketing hero. Uploading person/clothing/pose inputs, opening optional workspace tools and generating are distinct required task actions. Advanced actions are collapsed; real keyboard and pointer tests cover the visible controls.

The try-on route is an application form with selected references and retained generation results. Natural document scrolling keeps the complete workflow reachable on small screens and with expanded settings. A fixed marketing-screen height previously caused nested-scroll and hidden-action problems.

This application workspace deliberately scrolls as one document. Its form, reference board, optional settings and retained results must remain reachable at zoom and mobile widths; restricting it to a single marketing fold would recreate the usability issue the user asked to fix.
